EventItemActionText:
The Board of Architectural Review met in a regular session on Thursday, July 17, 2025, at 7:30 p.m. in Town Hall, 127 Center St S, Vienna, VA 22180.
Roll Call: Mr. Penati, Ms. Couchman, and Ms. Hanley were present. 

Absent Members: Ms. Shelly and Mr. O’Keefe.

Staff present: Planner Sharmaine Abaied and Board Clerk Yaska Camacho Castillo.

: Request for approval of a new single sliding door for Cedar Lane Shopping Center c/o First Washington Realty, located at 264E Cedar Ln SE, Docket No. PF-1763535-BAR, in the GS, Gateway South zoning district, filed by William Norton, Project 308 Design, Project Contact.

Applicant present: William Norton 

The applicant stated that as part of the landlord's work prior to the new tenant's move-in, they are required to replace the two existing swinging doors with a single sliding door assembly. The current doors are made of clear anodized aluminum painted black with a matte finish, originally thought to be dark bronze. A nearby Dollar Tree has a similar door specification but uses a double sliding door instead of a single. 

Mr. Penati made a motion to approve a new single sliding door for Cedar Lane Shopping Center c/o First Washington Realty, located at 264E Cedar Ln SE, Docket No. PF-1763535-BAR, in the GS, Gateway South zoning district, filed by William Norton, Project 308 Design, Project Contact with the following condition:

• Approved as noted on the plans to match the black color with the existing surroundings. 

Motion: Mr. Penati 
Second: Ms. Couchman 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 264 E Cedar Ln SE - Cedar Park Shopping Center - Exterior Modification

EventItemActionText:
Request approval of window signs for Pure Green, located at 136 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1683249-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district; filed by William Zaklis, of Pure Green, Business Owner.

Applicants present: William Zaklis & Elena Zaklis 

Mr. Zaklis stated that they already have a lighted sign installed, measuring 30" by 30".  It's made of vinyl and contains 30 LEDs, each producing approximately 90 lumens, as stated in the application. Previously, there were additional sticker graphics above the sign, visible from outside, but all have been removed except for one section. The remaining part only displays the words “smoothie” and “crafted smoothies,” with all surrounding stickers cut away.

One of the board members raised a concern about the sign potentially being in a pathway and therefore not ADA-compliant, unless a table were placed underneath it. The applicant clarified that, while there was no table at the time the photo was taken, there is one there now. However, the sign is mounted directly against the glass, so there is no pathway beneath it. Ms. Hanley noted that, although this issue may not fall within the board’s formal purview, the comment is being shared in the spirit of helpfulness.

Ms. Couchman made a motion to approve the window signs for Pure Green, located at 136 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1683249-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district; filed by William Zaklis, of Pure Green, Business Owner, as submitted. 

Motion: Ms. Couchman
Second: Mr. Penati 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 136 Maple Ave W - Pure Green - Signs

EventItemActionText:
Request approval of outdoor seating: chairs, tables, and planter boxes, for Pizza Vienna, located at 235 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-1191889-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district; filed by Ravi Johal, of Pizza Vienna, Business Owner.

Applicant present: Ijaz Raj

There was a discussion about the spacing and placement of planters or barriers in front of the store. There was a suggestion that the spacing between them should be at least 3 to 3.5 feet. It was advised not to overcrowd the space; possibly only 2 or 3 large pieces are needed, especially to maintain standing room and avoid blocking the main aisle or entrance. Even numbers are preferred for symmetry, and placement should not obstruct the entry. Depending on the size of the pieces (e.g., 38 inches), they could be placed one or two on each side of the entrance.

Ms. Hanley suggested aligning the planter specifications with existing outdoor dining guidelines to simplify decision-making. She stated that the board could craft a motion that requires compliance with those guidelines, allowing staff to handle the details. There's also a suggestion to stick with the originally proposed color (black), matching neighboring business Brusters, and to have staff review the final location and number of planters to keep the process straightforward.

Lastly, she mentioned that the planters, if kept outside year-round, should always contain something visually appealing even in winter, not dead or empty plants. The suggestions included small evergreens for winter and seasonal decorations like pumpkins for Halloween. These expectations align with the existing outdoor dining guidelines, which outline these aesthetic standards. 

Mr. Penati made a motion to approve the request for outdoor seating, chairs, tables, and planter box for Pizza Vienna located at 235 Maple Ave E, Dock at number PF-1191889-B AR in the AC Ave. Center Zoning District. Filed by Ravi Johal of Pizza Vienna with the following conditions
• The planter boxes are to follow the outdoor guidelines set by the town.
• The colors and other things as stated on the record are ok.

Motion: Mr. Penati
Second: Ms. Couchman 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 235 Maple Ave E - Pizza Vienna - Outdoor Dining

EventItemActionText:
Request approval of outdoor dining: tables, benches, umbrellas, and planter boxes for Bruster’s, located at 237 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-1683825-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by Mohammed Tariq, business owner.

Mr. Mohammed stated that they’re seeking approval for the outdoor seatings, which are two benches, two tables, and planters.

Ms. Hanley pointed out an error in the scale of a drawing, noting that it's labeled as 2 feet, but each box on the graph paper actually represents half a foot, so it needs correction. She also raised concerns about bench placement, noting the distance between benches may not meet Public Works requirements.

There are accessibility considerations, including ensuring a 3-foot-wide path from an ADA ramp to the customer entry. Additional concerns include pedestrian flow around a pillar, nearby parking spaces, and safety issues if people are seated with their backs facing traffic. Despite these issues, she complimented the colorful tables and chairs, saying they match the business's logo and are fitting for the prominent corner location.

Ms. Hanley suggested relying on town staff to ensure the site layout aligns with outdoor dining guidelines, including ADA compliance. She prefers not to set exact dimensions due to uncertainty about the accuracy of the existing site plan, especially the ADA ramp's location. Instead, she proposes having Public Works inspect the site, provide exact measurements (e.g., maintaining a 3-foot accessible path), and make small on-site adjustments as needed. This approach would ensure accuracy and compliance without overcomplicating the process.
The applicants sought clarification about the main concern regarding the layout. They are asking whether the issue is primarily the planters potentially interfering with parking spaces, or if the bigger concern is actually the round tables positioned within the area. 

Ms. Hanley responded that the current planter placement is acceptable, though ideally, a third planter behind the bench would be preferred. However, Mr. Penati noted that the existing sketch is inaccurate; it doesn’t clearly reflect key features like the building, ADA ramps, columns, and parking spaces. This makes it difficult to assess the layout properly. The board requests a to-scale, more accurate site drawing to better evaluate and plan the space.
Further discussion centered on the business initially wanting to install bollards for safety, but the landlord rejected that option due to lease restrictions. Planters were considered instead, though they take up more space. It's confirmed that benches have mounting plates and can be bolted, and there's openness to using benches as a substitute for planters, possibly facing inward for protection and visual boundaries.

There’s a broader concern about ensuring safety and visibility for both pedestrians and customers, especially due to unusual traffic patterns caused by double ADA ramps. Some non-permanent bollard alternatives (like large concrete blocks) are mentioned, but no final solution is identified. The board agrees that further exploration is needed to find a balance between safety, usability, and spatial limitations.

The applicant asked if they could have 4 benches instead, and Mr. Penati clarified that the issue isn't with the benches or tables themselves, but rather their placement and how it affects public access and required clearances. The area appears to be too crowded based on the current sketch. He said that the board is open to the setup if it can be shown to meet code requirements, but emphasized that they can't make a final judgment without a to-scale, accurate drawing. The concern is purely about ensuring proper spacing and compliance, not the type or design of the furniture.

There was a discussion about the 3-foot space between the door and the pillars under the awning, which is only meant for employee access, not customer seating or queuing.  The applicant stated that a bench can't fit in that area without blocking the employee entrance, so it's not a viable seating location.

Ms. Hanley brainstorms whether using space closer to the building (without obstructing the door) could offer benefits, like shade and better use of space, especially since customers primarily use the walk-up window, not the door.

The applicant clarified that employees mostly use the back entrance, and the intent is to have customer access flow from the ADA ramp to the window, with seating arranged elsewhere to avoid congestion and maintain safety. The discussion continued. 

The applicant suggested collaborating with Pizza Vienna to match planter colors and maintain a cohesive, seasonal aesthetic. 

For now, the board proposed approving the planter and seating area on the right-hand side, near Pizza Vienna, where there's no safety concern and enough space. They’re open to either benches or a table in that area, as long as it follows outdoor dining guidelines.

However, everything on the left side still needs to be resolved. When the business returns with a revised plan, it should include a to-scale drawing showing exact dimensions, locations of the ADA ramp, pickup window, and existing conditions, ensuring 3 feet of clearance throughout. Once that’s provided, the full setup can potentially be approved.

Ms. Couchman made a motion to approve the request for outdoor dining: tables, benches, umbrellas, and planter boxes for Bruster’s, located at 237 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-1683825
BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by Mohammed Tariq, business owner, with the following conditions:
• The logos are to be removed from the umbrellas.
• The benches on the left side of the ADA ramp are approved, pending staff review of their location behind the columns on the east side of the building.
• Collaborate with staff to provide a scaled site drawing.

Motion: Ms. Couchman
Second: Mr. Penati
Motino Carried
EventItemTitle: 237 Maple Ave E - Brusters - Outdoor Dining

EventItemActionText:
Request approval of new roof shingles for Train, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1604266-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Commercial Zoning district, filed by Paul Daniel, Ace Signs, project contact.

The applicant stated that he previously appeared before the Board, and during that meeting, Board members raised concerns about the existing brown roof, suggesting that a darker color would better align with the newly approved black-and-white color scheme. The idea of painting the existing asphalt shingles was discussed, though it was noted that this option might not hold up well over time and could require frequent maintenance. The applicant has revised the application and now proposes replacing the roof entirely with CertainTeed Landmark asphalt shingles in Charcoal Black. This change eliminates the need to paint the existing roof and offers a more durable, long-term solution that complements the approved exterior colors. Additionally, the applicant is also proposing to paint the monument black to match the roof.  The board did not have any concern.

Mr. Penati made a motion to approve the request for new roof shingles for Train, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1604266-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Commercial Zoning district, filed by Paul Daniel, Ace Signs, project contact, as submitted.

Motion: Mr. Penati
Second: Ms. Couchman
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 352 Maple Ave W - Train - Revision - Sign and Exterior Modification
